items.data_sentence: From each of 8 hysterectomy patients we sequenced RNA from 15 to 20 separate fibroids; TF motif priors and a protein interaction network are also available.
items.purpose_sentence: We want to know how each woman's fibroid regulatory network differs from those of the other women.
items.prompt: From each of 8 hysterectomy patients we sequenced RNA from 15 to 20 separate fibroids; TF motif priors and a protein interaction network are also available. We want to know how each woman's fibroid regulatory network differs from those of the other women.
must_include: Notes each woman contributed 15-20 fibroids, enough to estimate a network from her own samples
Offers an aggregate network per woman (e.g. PANDA or OTTER on her fibroids alone) and compares the eight
Uses the stated TF motif and PPI priors
red_flags: Claims per-woman networks need a per-sample method because aggregate workflows pool everyone
Pools all fibroids into one network and stops
Treats each fibroid as a separate individual

items.data_sentence: From each of 8 hysterectomy patients we sequenced RNA from 15 to 20 separate fibroids; TF motif priors and a protein interaction network are also available.
items.purpose_sentence: Do the fibroid networks of the four premenopausal women differ from those of the four postmenopausal women?
items.prompt: From each of 8 hysterectomy patients we sequenced RNA from 15 to 20 separate fibroids; TF motif priors and a protein interaction network are also available. Do the fibroid networks of the four premenopausal women differ from those of the four postmenopausal women?
must_include: Treats the woman as the replicate: four versus four, so power is limited
Builds per-woman (or per-group) networks and compares the two menopausal groups
red_flags: Treats the 60-80 fibroids per group as independent replicates
Ranks individual women instead of answering the group question

items.data_sentence: From each of 8 hysterectomy patients we sequenced RNA from 15 to 20 separate fibroids; TF motif priors and a protein interaction network are also available.

items.prompt: From each of 8 hysterectomy patients we sequenced RNA from 15 to 20 separate fibroids; TF motif priors and a protein interaction network are also available. For now we only need a description of the regulatory network operating in these fibroids.
must_include: One aggregate TF-gene network over the fibroids answers this
No comparison, test or per-sample network is needed
red_flags: Insists on per-sample or per-woman networks
Adds a hypothesis test or comparison the user did not ask for

items.data_sentence: From each of 8 hysterectomy patients we sequenced RNA from 15 to 20 separate fibroids; TF motif priors and a protein interaction network are also available.
items.purpose_sentence: Which transcription factors differ most in activity between the women, independent of their own mRNA levels?
items.prompt: From each of 8 hysterectomy patients we sequenced RNA from 15 to 20 separate fibroids; TF motif priors and a protein interaction network are also available. Which transcription factors differ most in activity between the women, independent of their own mRNA levels?
must_include: Activity apart from a TF's own mRNA needs a TF-activity estimate (GIRAFFE), not targeting or expression
Summarises each woman's TF activity from her 15-20 fibroids and compares the women

items.data_sentence: Six women collected a fingerprick blood sample every morning across two full menstrual cycles; we have only RNA-seq counts, plus the cycle day of each sample.
items.purpose_sentence: Which of the six women shows the largest co-expression shift between her follicular and luteal phases?
items.prompt: Six women collected a fingerprick blood sample every morning across two full menstrual cycles; we have only RNA-seq counts, plus the cycle day of each sample. Which of the six women shows the largest co-expression shift between her follicular and luteal phases?
must_include: Each woman has roughly 28 daily samples per phase, enough for her own phase-specific co-expression
Compares phases within each woman, then ranks the six women
Stays with expression-only workflows
red_flags: Says per-woman estimation is impossible and only per-sample networks can answer it
Proposes workflows that need TF motif or PPI priors
Answers with one pooled phase comparison across all women

items.data_sentence: Six women collected a fingerprick blood sample every morning across two full menstrual cycles; we have only RNA-seq counts, plus the cycle day of each sample.
items.purpose_sentence: Across the six women, does blood co-expression differ between the follicular and luteal phases?
items.prompt: Six women collected a fingerprick blood sample every morning across two full menstrual cycles; we have only RNA-seq counts, plus the cycle day of each sample. Across the six women, does blood co-expression differ between the follicular and luteal phases?
must_include: Recognises the paired design: the same six women in both phases
Estimates the phase effect within women or adjusts for woman (e.g. COBRA with phase and woman covariates)
red_flags: Treats the roughly 340 daily samples as independent replicates
Proposes motif- or PPI-based workflows despite expression-only data

items.data_sentence: Six women collected a fingerprick blood sample every morning across two full menstrual cycles; we have only RNA-seq counts, plus the cycle day of each sample.
items.purpose_sentence: For now we just want to map the co-expression network in each woman's blood, without comparing anything.
items.prompt: Six women collected a fingerprick blood sample every morning across two full menstrual cycles; we have only RNA-seq counts, plus the cycle day of each sample. For now we just want to map the co-expression network in each woman's blood, without comparing anything.
must_include: Each woman's daily samples support a co-expression network of her own
No comparison or test is needed
red_flags: Invents a phase or between-woman comparison
Requires TF motif or PPI priors

items.data_sentence: Six women collected a fingerprick blood sample every morning across two full menstrual cycles; we have only RNA-seq counts, plus the cycle day of each sample.
items.purpose_sentence: We suspect one or two participants are wired differently from the rest and want to spot them.
items.prompt: Six women collected a fingerprick blood sample every morning across two full menstrual cycles; we have only RNA-seq counts, plus the cycle day of each sample. We suspect one or two participants are wired differently from the rest and want to spot them.
must_include: Reads this as finding outlying individuals among the six women
Each woman's many daily samples allow a network per woman to compare against the others
red_flags: Answers with a cohort-level phase comparison

items.data_sentence: We have RNA-seq and DNA methylation arrays on the same 300 postmortem white-matter blocks, lesions and normal-appearing tissue, from 15 multiple sclerosis brain donors.
items.purpose_sentence: We want to know how each donor's methylation-expression network differs from the other donors'.
items.prompt: We have RNA-seq and DNA methylation arrays on the same 300 postmortem white-matter blocks, lesions and normal-appearing tissue, from 15 multiple sclerosis brain donors. We want to know how each donor's methylation-expression network differs from the other donors'.
must_include: Each donor gave about 20 blocks, enough for a two-layer network per donor
Keeps methylation and expression together in one two-layer network
Notes each donor's lesion/normal block mix can confound donor differences
red_flags: Drops methylation and builds expression-only networks
Claims per-donor networks are only possible with a per-sample method
Treats each block as a separate individual

items.data_sentence: We have RNA-seq and DNA methylation arrays on the same 300 postmortem white-matter blocks, lesions and normal-appearing tissue, from 15 multiple sclerosis brain donors.
items.purpose_sentence: Across donors, does methylation-expression coupling differ between lesions and normal-appearing white matter?
items.prompt: We have RNA-seq and DNA methylation arrays on the same 300 postmortem white-matter blocks, lesions and normal-appearing tissue, from 15 multiple sclerosis brain donors. Across donors, does methylation-expression coupling differ between lesions and normal-appearing white matter?
must_include: Paired design: lesion and normal-appearing blocks come from the same donors; the donor is the replicate
Compares two-layer networks of the two tissue types within donors
red_flags: Treats the 300 blocks as independent replicates
Ignores the methylation layer

items.data_sentence: We have RNA-seq and DNA methylation arrays on the same 300 postmortem white-matter blocks, lesions and normal-appearing tissue, from 15 multiple sclerosis brain donors.
items.purpose_sentence: As a first step we only want one integrated methylation-expression network across all the blocks.
items.prompt: We have RNA-seq and DNA methylation arrays on the same 300 postmortem white-matter blocks, lesions and normal-appearing tissue, from 15 multiple sclerosis brain donors. As a first step we only want one integrated methylation-expression network across all the blocks.
must_include: One aggregate two-layer network across all blocks answers this
No per-donor or per-block networks are needed
red_flags: Insists on per-sample or per-donor networks
Builds two separate single-layer networks instead of one joint network

items.data_sentence: We have RNA-seq and DNA methylation arrays on the same 300 postmortem white-matter blocks, lesions and normal-appearing tissue, from 15 multiple sclerosis brain donors.
items.purpose_sentence: We do not need anything per donor; do progressive-onset donors differ from relapsing-onset donors in methylation-expression coupling?
items.prompt: We have RNA-seq and DNA methylation arrays on the same 300 postmortem white-matter blocks, lesions and normal-appearing tissue, from 15 multiple sclerosis brain donors. We do not need anything per donor; do progressive-onset donors differ from relapsing-onset donors in methylation-expression coupling?
must_include: Respects that per-donor results are not wanted
Notes the donor is still the replicate for the progressive versus relapsing test (15 donors)
Uses a two-layer method
red_flags: Delivers per-donor networks or rankings as the answer
Treats the 300 blocks as independent samples in the group test

items.data_sentence: From 22 heart failure patients we have left ventricular tissue at assist-device implantation and at transplant, with mRNA and miRNA sequencing, TF motif and miRNA-target priors, and PPI.
items.purpose_sentence: Which patients' cardiac regulatory networks remodelled most during device support?
items.prompt: From 22 heart failure patients we have left ventricular tissue at assist-device implantation and at transplant, with mRNA and miRNA sequencing, TF motif and miRNA-target priors, and PPI. Which patients' cardiac regulatory networks remodelled most during device support?
must_include: Only one sample per patient per time point, so a network per patient needs per-sample estimation
Ranks patients by the change between their implant and transplant sample networks
red_flags: Runs an aggregate network per patient from two samples
Answers from two cohort-level networks (implant versus transplant) only

items.data_sentence: From 22 heart failure patients we have left ventricular tissue at assist-device implantation and at transplant, with mRNA and miRNA sequencing, TF motif and miRNA-target priors, and PPI.
items.purpose_sentence: Across the cohort, did cardiac gene regulation change between implantation and transplant?
items.prompt: From 22 heart failure patients we have left ventricular tissue at assist-device implantation and at transplant, with mRNA and miRNA sequencing, TF motif and miRNA-target priors, and PPI. Across the cohort, did cardiac gene regulation change between implantation and transplant?
must_include: Recognises the paired design: the same 22 patients at two time points
Answers at the cohort level, e.g. a network per time point or a paired test on per-sample networks
red_flags: Treats the two time points as independent groups
Gives patient-by-patient rankings instead of a cohort answer

items.data_sentence: From 22 heart failure patients we have left ventricular tissue at assist-device implantation and at transplant, with mRNA and miRNA sequencing, TF motif and miRNA-target priors, and PPI.
items.purpose_sentence: For now we only want the combined TF and microRNA regulatory network of these hearts.
items.prompt: From 22 heart failure patients we have left ventricular tissue at assist-device implantation and at transplant, with mRNA and miRNA sequencing, TF motif and miRNA-target priors, and PPI. For now we only want the combined TF and microRNA regulatory network of these hearts.
must_include: Includes miRNA regulators by using the miRNA-target prior
One aggregate network is enough
red_flags: Drops the miRNAs and builds a TF-only network
Adds a before/after or per-patient analysis that was not asked for

items.data_sentence: From 22 heart failure patients we have left ventricular tissue at assist-device implantation and at transplant, with mRNA and miRNA sequencing, TF motif and miRNA-target priors, and PPI.

items.prompt: From 22 heart failure patients we have left ventricular tissue at assist-device implantation and at transplant, with mRNA and miRNA sequencing, TF motif and miRNA-target priors, and PPI. Which microRNAs change their targeting most between the two operations?
must_include: Needs a miRNA-aware workflow that uses the miRNA-target prior
Compares the two operations as a paired design
red_flags: Recommends TF-only workflows (PANDA, LIONESS-PANDA, OTTER, GIRAFFE) for a miRNA question

items.data_sentence: One healthy volunteer has given venous blood every week for three years; we have RNA-seq for all 150 draws, human TF motif priors and a PPI network.

items.data_sentence: From each of 11 familial adenomatous polyposis colectomies we sequenced 20 to 30 adenomas plus five normal mucosa samples, with TF motif priors and a PPI network.

items.data_sentence: From each of 8 laying hens we sequenced about 30 ovarian follicles of varying size, with only RNA-seq data and the diameter of every follicle.

items.data_sentence: We have kidney biopsy RNA-seq from 130 patients with IgA nephropathy, TF motif priors, a PPI network, and five-year follow-up of kidney function.
items.purpose_sentence: We want to predict, from regulatory features of each patient's biopsy, who will progress to kidney failure.
items.prompt: We have kidney biopsy RNA-seq from 130 patients with IgA nephropathy, TF motif priors, a PPI network, and five-year follow-up of kidney function. We want to predict, from regulatory features of each patient's biopsy, who will progress to kidney failure.
must_include: One biopsy per patient, so patient-level features need per-sample estimation (sample networks or TF activity)

red_flags: Uses one aggregate network, or two outcome-group networks, as the predictor
Presents network edges as causal drivers of progression

items.data_sentence: We sequenced liver, kidney, heart and lung from 80 laboratory rats, but each rat gave only one of the four tissues; TF motif priors and a PPI network are available.
items.purpose_sentence: Which rats have unusual regulatory networks compared with others of the same tissue?
items.prompt: We sequenced liver, kidney, heart and lung from 80 laboratory rats, but each rat gave only one of the four tissues; TF motif priors and a PPI network are available. Which rats have unusual regulatory networks compared with others of the same tissue?
must_include: Each rat gave one sample, so per-rat networks require per-sample estimation
Compares rats within a tissue (about 20 per tissue), not across tissues
red_flags: Assumes four tissues per rat and builds per-rat aggregate networks
